title: External resources don't have a fallback mechanism

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Websites can be made up out of many different resources, hosted by different providers.

The page itself might be rendered by a specific server and assets like stylesheets might be served by a separate CDN.

In such configurations only part of the hosting providers might suffer an outage.
(As what happend with Cloudflare today)

Often it is possible to host assets in multiple locations but swapping the `href` values for large websites is much more complex.

Web pages will often have server side cache and invalidating the entire cache to swap the `href` value might do more harm than good.

Ideally there is some mechanism to communicate alternative locations for resources.

### What solutions exist today?

This is somewhat possible today:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.com/style.css"
  onerror="this.onerror=null;this.href='https://example.com/style.css';"
/>
```

But this solution is bit gnarly.

A dedicated API/feature would be easier to implement and easier to document/teach

### How would you solve it?

My current preference is to be able to describe a separate external resource and define that one is a fallback for the other.

The fallback resource is only loaded when the first one fails to load.

Something like:

```html
<link id="my-styles" rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.com/style.css" />
<link fallback-for="my-styles" rel="stylesheet" href="https://example.com/style.css" />
```



### Anything else?

_No response_
